summary: Sarah kneads flour measured in seahs, and Abigail takes roasted grain measured the same way. At Samaria’s gate the price of a seah of flour marks the end of the famine.

senses.definition: A unit of capacity for dry goods, whether grain, roasted kernels or flour.

evidence.note: Abraham asks Sarah to knead three seahs of fine flour for the visitors.
Abigail packs five seahs of roasted grain among the provisions for David.
The trench around Elijah’s altar is described by reference to two seahs of seed.
Elisha announces that one seah of fine flour and two seahs of barley will each sell for a shekel.
When the people plunder the Aramean camp, flour and barley sell at the announced prices.
The narrator repeats the two quantities and their common price at the city gate.
A woman mixes leaven into three measures of flour.
The same parable gives the quantity of flour in three sata.

evidence.locator: s.v. sʾh, sʾtʾ, especially IduOstr 1:3.3 and QumNJ 2:4::4
pp. 43–45, vessel inscription a, st followed by three strokes

note: The expression in 1Ki.18.32 may describe the trench’s capacity or the area sown with two seahs of seed. Röllig reads Phoenician st on a vessel as the name of this measure. The inscription lacks the medial aleph found in Hebrew and Aramaic.
